label: Generalized Hermite and Laguerre Polynomials
notes: This appendix lifts two classical orthogonal polynomial systems from the real line to a symmetric matrix argument. We motivate why the noncentral distributions of latent roots on special manifolds demand such polynomials, and we preview orthogonality against the matrix-variate normal and Wishart weights as the organizing thread of the lecture.

label: Why Matrix-Argument Polynomials
notes: Latent root distributions arising from noncentral Wishart matrices are awkward zonal-polynomial series. By expanding them in polynomials orthogonal to the relevant weight we obtain coefficients that decouple, converge faster, and expose the noncentrality structure. This slide frames the practical payoff that motivates the whole construction.

label: Univariate Hermite Recap
notes: We recall the scalar Hermite polynomials orthogonal to the standard Gaussian weight, their three-term recurrence, and the Rodrigues formula. These are the seeds every matrix generalization must reduce to when the argument collapses to a one-by-one matrix, so the audience should hold them as the limiting checkpoint.

label: Univariate Laguerre Recap
notes: The generalized Laguerre polynomials are orthogonal to the gamma weight on the positive half line, indexed by a shape parameter alpha. They are the eigenvalue-level building block for the Wishart case, and their weight is exactly the density of a chi-square scaled variable, which we will lift to the Wishart density.

label: Orthogonality as Inner Product
notes: Orthogonality means the weighted inner product of two polynomials of distinct degree vanishes. We visualize the Gram matrix becoming diagonal under the correct weight. This geometric picture, inner product equals zero off the diagonal, is the single idea that survives intact when we pass to a matrix argument.

label: Matrix-Variate Normal Weight
notes: The generalized Hermite polynomials are orthogonal with respect to the matrix-variate normal density on symmetric matrices. We write the weight, identify the trace quadratic form in the exponent, and note that integration runs over the cone of symmetric matrices with the invariant measure used throughout the book.

label: Generalized Hermite Polynomials
notes: Generalized Hermite polynomials are indexed by partitions and built from zonal polynomials of the matrix argument. We give the leading zonal term and the matrix Rodrigues formula using repeated differentiation against the normal weight, emphasizing that the partition index replaces the single degree of the scalar theory.

label: Wishart Weight and Laguerre
notes: Generalized Laguerre polynomials are orthogonal to the Wishart density on positive definite matrices, indexed by partitions and carrying the dimension parameter through the multivariate gamma. We point out that the shape parameter of the scalar Laguerre becomes the Wishart degrees of freedom in the matrix lift.

label: Generating Functions
notes: Both families admit generating functions written as hypergeometric functions of matrix argument with two matrix slots. Expanding the kernel in zonal polynomials and matching partition coefficients recovers the individual polynomials. This is the most efficient route to explicit low-order polynomials and to their orthogonality constants.

label: Orthogonality over the Matrix Cone
notes: We state the full orthogonality relation: integrating two generalized polynomials of distinct partition against the matrix weight over the cone gives zero, and the diagonal gives an explicit normalization built from multivariate gamma values. The schematic shows the Gram structure indexed by partitions becoming block diagonal.

label: Expanding Noncentral Distributions
notes: The payoff: the noncentral Wishart latent root density expands in generalized Laguerre polynomials, with coefficients that are simple functions of the noncentrality matrix eigenvalues. Truncating the series yields practical approximations whose error we can monitor, closing the loop from motivation to computation.

label: Summary and Checkpoints
notes: We recap the dictionary: Gaussian weight to matrix normal gives Hermite, gamma weight to Wishart gives Laguerre, degree to partition, recurrence to zonal expansion. We restate the reduction checks at dimension one and list the orthogonality and generating-function identities students should be able to reproduce.
